newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen to receive two Airbus A300s in March.
newsitem.headline: Yemen to receive two Airbus A300s in March.

text.p: Yemen's national carrier Yemen Airways will receive two Airbus A300s from manufacturer Airbus Industrie in March, the English-language newspaper Yemen Times said in its latest weekly issue.
The Sanaa-based airline was formed last year by the merger of Yemenia Airways and al-Yemda -- the carriers of the former North Yemen and South Yemen which merged in 1990.
Saudi Arabia's national carrier Saudi Arabian Airlines holds a 49 percent stake in Yemen Airways.
The Yemeni airline has a fleet of 12 aircraft -- four Boeing 727s, one Boeing 707 three Boeing 737s, three de Havilland Dash-7s one Airbus A310.

Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
